events.title: Buena Vista Social Club — Broadway in Orlando
events.venue: Dr. Phillips Center — Walt Disney Theater
events.blurb: The Tony- and Grammy-winning Broadway musical built on the legendary Cuban album closes its Orlando run this weekend — live musicians on stage and all that irresistible Havana rhythm. Dinner downtown, then the show: a proper big date night.

events.title: Crooked Can Oktoberfest
events.venue: Crooked Can Brewing · Plant St. Market
events.blurb: Oktoberfest weekend at Winter Garden's anchor brewery — craft pours, German-style food specials from the Plant St. Market vendors, and live entertainment on the patio. Easy to pair with dinner or a Plant Street stroll.

events.title: Boo at the Zoo
events.blurb: Daytime trick-or-treating among the animals, with themed treat stations, decorations, and performances — all the Halloween fun, none of the after-dark scares. Also on Oct 31.

events.title: Brick-or-Treat Monster Party
events.blurb: A full theme-park day wrapped in not-scary Halloween: a trick-or-treat street of LEGO monster houses, character meet-and-greets, and an evening drone show. Designed for ages 2–12 — rides in the morning, candy trail after nap. Also Oct 25 & 30.

events.title: Gators, Ghosts & Goblins at Gatorland
events.blurb: Gatorland's daytime, not-so-scary Halloween send-off: trick-or-treating, a kids' costume parade, Skunk Ape and Eddie the Yeti meet-and-greets, and the Cryptid Express — all included with admission ($31.99 adult / $22.99 child 3–12 online), on top of the gators and splash pad.

events.title: Guppyween — Sensory-Friendly Morning
events.blurb: A special sensory-friendly Guppyween session with softer lights and sounds — a uniquely gentle first Halloween outing for a 3-year-old, before the regular crowds arrive.

events.title: Zoo Boo Bash at Central Florida Zoo
events.blurb: The zoo's not-so-scary daytime Halloween party: treat stations, costumes, seasonal animal enrichment, and character meet-and-greets (Anna, Elsa & Kristoff Oct 24–25; the Sanderson Sisters Oct 31). Included with regular zoo admission; pass holders $5.

events.title: Celebration Farmers Market
events.blurb: A Sunday-morning market along Front Street in Celebration's storybook Town Center — farm-fresh produce, handmade goods, and local vendors, with lakeside paths and porch rocking chairs for a slow family morning.

events.title: Fall Festival at Southern Hill Farms
events.note: Online only — buy by night before & save $1
events.blurb: The 11th annual fall festival at the Clermont blueberry farm: corn maze, petting zoo, farm wagon rides, a covered playground, u-pick sunflower and zinnia fields, live music, and the famous apple cider donuts. Tickets are online only for ages 3+ (2 and under free) — Sunday hours are 9 to 7, an easy full morning with a toddler.

events.title: $5 Halloween Flix: Poltergeist
events.blurb: The Garden Theatre's Tuesday Halloween series closes with Poltergeist in the restored 1930s movie palace on Plant Street — budget-friendly concessions and just the right amount of spooky for a Tuesday date night.

events.title: Live Trivia at Crooked Can
events.blurb: Live team trivia on the brewery's main patio every Tuesday — four rounds, a movie-of-the-week halftime quiz, and a Jeopardy-style final, with gift-card prizes. Order from the Plant St. Market counters and make it dinner-and-a-game.

events.title: Preschool Storytime — Windermere Library
events.blurb: A weekly preschool storytime at the little Windermere branch on Main Street: picture books, songs, and rhymes that build early literacy, designed for ages 3–5. Two minutes from home — the perfect standing Thursday plan.

events.title: Fridays on the Plaza — Live Music
events.blurb: Winter Garden's year-round Friday ritual: a free live set under the Centennial Plaza gazebo while Plant Street hums with dinner crowds. Grab a table nearby, then wander over with dessert or a glass of wine.

events.title: Brick-or-Treat Monster Party
events.blurb: A full theme-park day wrapped in not-scary Halloween: a trick-or-treat street of LEGO monster houses, character meet-and-greets, and an evening drone show. Designed for ages 2–12 — rides in the morning, candy trail after nap. Also Oct 25 & 30.

events.title: Halloween Spookquarium
events.blurb: Trick-or-treat stations throughout the aquarium, with rescued dolphins and sea turtles as your hosts — a sweet late-afternoon Halloween stop if you're already Gulf-side.

events.title: BooChella at Millie Moo's
events.blurb: A mini music-festival-style Halloween party for little kids inside Millie Moo's play space — costumes, music, sweet treats, and bubbles with fog, all deliberately not-so-scary for the preschool crowd.

events.title: Windermere Farmers Market
events.blurb: Windermere's own Friday-morning market on Main Street — produce, seafood, breads and pastries, coffee, honey, flowers, and crafts under the oaks. An easy weekly ritual with a toddler: snack, stroll, say hi to the neighbors.

events.title: Winter Garden Halloween Light Show
events.blurb: A family-friendly Halloween projection show splashed across the front of Winter Garden City Hall, looping to spooky tunes on Plant Street. Low-key and perfect for a toddler — stroll up, watch from the sidewalk, grab a treat from a nearby café.

events.title: OSC After Dark — Halloween at Orlando Science Center
events.note: 21+ only · includes open bar · costumes encouraged
events.blurb: Halloween night, kid-free: the Science Center opens after dark for a 21+ fundraiser with an open bar, a Monster Mash dance party in DinoDigs, a costume contest, laser show, karaoke, and telescope time in the observatory. The grown-up Halloween party — book the sitter.

events.title: Boo-tanical Bash at Bok Tower Gardens
events.blurb: A not-so-scary garden party on Halloween morning: a kids' concert from the 60-bell Singing Tower, a Monster Mash dance party, pumpkin painting, and a live Jack and the Beanstalk show. Wraps by 2 PM — home well before the evening crowds.

events.note: Last entry 4:00 PM · Saturdays & Sundays thru Nov 15
events.blurb: Old-fashioned farm fun in Mount Dora: a 7-acre corn maze (plus smaller mazes for little kids), a jumping pillow, a 60-foot super slide, a castle playground, tractor farm tours, and a pumpkin patch, with the farm market and café next door. Saturdays and Sundays only, through November 15.

events.title: Guppyween at The Florida Aquarium
events.note: Costumed kids free with a paid adult (ticket window)
events.blurb: Halloween built for the littlest monsters: costumed divers carve pumpkins underwater while kids trick-or-treat past the tanks. Also runs Oct 25 & 31.

events.title: Hawks and Haunts at Audubon Center for Birds of Prey
events.venue: Audubon Center for Birds of Prey
events.blurb: A daytime Halloween party at the raptor rescue center on Lake Sybelia: a 'trick-or-tweet' candy trail, bubble dance party, kid-friendly story time, a scavenger hunt, and meet-and-greets with eagles, owls, and hawks. $10 per person; children 3 and under free.

events.title: Free Day & Story Time at Leu Gardens
events.blurb: On the first Monday of each month Leu Gardens waives admission and hosts story time and songs with librarians — then spend the rest of the day wandering the lush, stroller-friendly gardens.

events.title: Monty Python's Spamalot — Broadway in Orlando
events.venue: Dr. Phillips Center — Walt Disney Theater
events.note: Runs Tue Nov 3 – Thu Nov 5 only
events.blurb: A three-night-only Broadway stop: Spamalot, the Monty Python musical 'lovingly ripped off' from the Holy Grail film, brings killer rabbits, French taunters, and the Knights Who Say Ni to the Walt Disney Theater. Silly in the best way — an easy midweek date.

events.title: Free Friday Evening at the Morse Museum
events.venue: Charles Hosmer Morse Museum of American Art
events.note: Free Fridays Nov–Apr · first of the season
events.blurb: The Morse Museum's beloved free Friday evenings return for the season: admission is free from 4 to 8 PM, with the galleries — including the Tiffany Chapel and the world's most comprehensive Tiffany collection — open late. Pair it with dinner on Park Avenue for an easy Winter Park date, or bring the family before bedtime.

events.title: MAX POWER at Kennedy Space Center
events.note: Astronaut parade Sat & Sun 3:30 PM · Thunderbirds Nov 7–8
events.blurb: NASA's biggest celebration weekend: astronaut meet-and-greets, hands-on S.T.E.A.M. activities, and a first-ever parade with astronauts riding in Corvettes. A big day out — anchor it around Planet Play and the parade, and bring the stroller.

events.title: Django Festival All-Stars at Judson's Live
events.note: Also Sun Nov 8 · intimate cabaret room
events.blurb: A night of gypsy jazz in the intimate Judson's Live cabaret room: the Django Festival All-Stars channel Django Reinhardt with blazing guitar, soaring violin, and accordion — the Wall Street Journal calls it 'the best jazz show in town.' Pick the 6:30 PM set, then dinner downtown.

events.title: Cows 'n Cabs — Winter Park Food & Wine Festival
events.note: Sells out annually · Tapas & 'Tinis night is Thu Nov 5
events.blurb: The 14th annual Cows 'n Cabs takes over Winter Park's West Meadow: 30+ Central Florida restaurants and 60+ wine, beer, and spirits vendors under the big tent, with live music — all benefiting charities for local children. It's the splurge date night of the fall, and it sells out every year.

events.title: Fall Wine Walk: Corks & Crowns at Bok Tower Gardens
events.blurb: An adults' afternoon in the Olmsted gardens: a fall wine walk through Bok Tower's grounds with the Singing Tower as backdrop. Worth the Lake Wales drive as a day-date — pair it with a garden stroll before the walk starts.

events.blurb: Downtown Orlando's longest-running fall tradition: hundreds of artist and crafter booths ringing Lake Eola, food vendors, live entertainment at the amphitheater, and an AdventHealth for Children Kids Zone. Free, stroller-friendly, and an easy morning-to-lunch outing with a toddler.
events.source: Fiesta in the Park / City of Orlando

events.title: Founders Day — Celebration's 30th Anniversary
events.blurb: Celebration turns 30 with a full-day hometown party: a morning parade from Lakeside Park to Founders Park, a 30th-anniversary town photo, and an evening celebration in Town Center. Festive and stroller-friendly, about 20 minutes away.

events.title: Maker Faire Orlando
events.note: Also Sun Nov 8 · Robot Ruckus can be loud
events.blurb: The 14th annual Maker Faire fills the fairgrounds with hands-on invention: robots, crafts, workshops, and things that spin, blink, and roll. It's a big, busy day — best in the morning with a toddler, and bring ear protection for the Robot Ruckus combat arena.

events.title: Asian Lantern Festival: Into the Wild — Opening Night
events.blurb: Opening night of the zoo's glowing nighttime lantern walk: a ¾-mile stroller-friendly loop of giant illuminated animals and a new solar-system display. Book the 6 PM entry — dark enough for the lights, early enough for a toddler bedtime.

events.title: ICE! featuring The Polar Express — Opening Weekend
events.note: 9° exhibit — parkas provided, bring warm layers
events.blurb: Opening weekend of ICE!: two million pounds of hand-carved ice retell The Polar Express at a bracing 9 degrees, with two-story ice slides. Blue parkas are provided — add hats, gloves, and thick socks for a toddler. Runs through Jan 3 as part of Christmas at Gaylord Palms.

events.title: Flavor Fest: A Taste of Horizon West
events.note: Ticket includes all samples · prices rise Nov 1
events.blurb: Horizon West's premier food night: dozens of local restaurants and drink vendors serving tapas-style samples on the Hamlin green, with live music. One ticket, all the tastings — come hungry and graze through the neighborhood's best kitchens.

events.title: Winter Park Autumn Art Festival
events.note: Also Sun Nov 15 · children's art workshop
events.blurb: The 53rd annual juried festival of Florida-only artists along Park Avenue: live music on the Central Park stage, a children's art workshop, food vendors, and a beer garden. A pretty stroller-and-stroll day trip — free admission.

events.title: Festival of Trees — Opening Weekend at Orlando Museum of Art
events.blurb: The 40th annual Festival of Trees turns the Orlando Museum of Art into a holiday showcase: 50+ designer-decorated trees, gingerbread creations, Santa Claus Lane, and weekend Santa photos. A gentle, stroller-friendly first taste of the holiday season — Breakfast with Santa (separate ticket) runs 8:30 AM this same morning.

events.title: Wild World of Animals at Garden Theatre
events.note: Pick the 1 PM matinee with a toddler
events.blurb: Grant Kemmerer's live wildlife show brings reptiles, birds, mammals, and other animals face-to-face with the audience in Winter Garden's historic theatre — part education, part comedy. The 1 PM matinee is the toddler-friendly pick.
events.source: Garden Theatre / City of Winter Garden

events.title: Winter Garden Farmers Market

events.title: Florida Coffee Festival at Festival Park
events.blurb: A Sunday tasting stroll for coffee people: roasters and cafés from around Florida pouring at Festival Park in the Milk District. Go late morning, sample your way around, and make it brunch in the Milk District after.

events.title: Manatee Season Begins at Blue Spring
events.blurb: The first official day of manatee season at Florida's most famous winter refuge, where several hundred manatees drift into the crystal-clear 72° spring run. The elevated boardwalk is stroller-friendly — arrive at opening, the park fills fast.

events.note: Runs Nov 14–22 · Breakfast with Santa 8:30 AM today

events.note: Selling quickly per Gaylord calendar · 3 & under free

events.title: Half-Price Tuesdays at Cinépolis Hamlin
events.blurb: Dinner-and-a-movie without the weekend markup: Cinépolis' luxury theater at Hamlin (recliners, dine-in service) cuts ticket prices in half every Tuesday. Pair with dinner in Hamlin Town Center.

events.title: Plant Street Market & Crooked Can Evening
events.blurb: The no-planning-needed downtown date: about 20 food and artisan vendors inside Plant Street Market, Crooked Can's taps at the center, and big patio seating under the lights. Go Friday or Saturday for the best scene, then walk Plant Street after.

events.title: Bok Tower Gardens + Hammock Hollow
events.blurb: Shady Olmsted-designed gardens built around a 205-foot Singing Tower, with Hammock Hollow Children's Garden — water play, a fairy garden, and sand and climbing play under the oaks. One of Florida's prettiest toddler days out.

events.title: Cocoa Beach Pier Day
events.timeLabel: Beach all day · pier from 11:00 AM
events.blurb: The classic Space Coast beach day: an 800-foot pier over the Atlantic with restaurants, rentals, and showers right at the sand. Morning is the toddler sweet spot — gentler waves, easier parking — and if a rocket launches, you'll see it from your beach blanket.

events.title: Kennedy Space Center + Planet Play
events.timeLabel: Daily 9:00 AM – 5:00 PM · arrive at opening
events.blurb: Stand under the space shuttle Atlantis, then let your toddler loose in Planet Play — a multi-story indoor playground of planets and climbing nets built for little kids while you grab a coffee. Mostly indoors and stroller-friendly; under-3s are free.

events.title: The Florida Aquarium
events.note: Bring swim gear for the splash pad
events.blurb: Sharks, penguins, and a wetlands trail under a glass dome — plus The Splash Pad, an outdoor water-play area made for toddlers. Under-3s get in free, and it's an easy pair with lunch in Sparkman Wharf next door.
